column3: NKJV has “come near Him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “bring him to Him.” “Pallet” is rendered “bed.”
NKJV has “speak blasphemies like this,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Why does this man speak thus? He blasphemes!”
Close to the Greek; “authority” is rendered “power.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV names “Levi's house,” where the Greek has “his house.”
NKJV has “the scribes and Pharisees” and “eats and drinks,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the scribes of the Pharisees” and “eats.”
NKJV includes “to repentance,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “but sinners.”
NKJV renders “the sons of the bridechamber” as “the friends of the bridegroom.”
NKJV has “in those days,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “in that day.”
NKJV has “the new wine bursts” and “the wine is spilled,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the wine will burst the wineskins, and the wine is destroyed.”
Close to the Greek; “the loaves of the presentation” is rendered “the showbread.”
